inspiration.observed_pattern: A PostgreSQL application updates user fields conditionally with CASE expressions and returns the changed user rows with RETURNING.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Combine those behaviors in an independently authored snapshot archive: INSERT ... SELECT uses CASE to map active users to live or paused labels, returns generated snapshot IDs, and preserves deterministic source order.

fixture_notes: Active Alice remains live while inactive Bob receives a paused label and state through CASE branches; both snapshots are returned with generated IDs.
determinism_notes: Fixed user IDs and statuses, explicit source ordering, and auto-increment snapshot IDs created in that order; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE users (user_id INT PRIMARY KEY, username VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, active TINYINT NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE user_snapshots (snapshot_id INT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY, user_id INT NOT NULL, display_label VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL, lifecycle_state VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL)

steps.sql: INSERT INTO user_snapshots (user_id, display_label, lifecycle_state) SELECT user_id, CASE WHEN active = 1 THEN username ELSE CONCAT(username, ' (paused)') END, CASE WHEN active = 1 THEN 'live' ELSE 'paused' END FROM users ORDER BY user_id RETURNING snapshot_id, user_id, display_label, lifecycle_state

checks.sql: SELECT snapshot_id, user_id, display_label, lifecycle_state FROM user_snapshots ORDER BY snapshot_id
SELECT user_id, username, active FROM users ORDER BY user_id
